title: Engineering All-Hands Notes - 2026-06-17
content:
Engineering All-Hands — Notes
Date: 2026-06-17
Owner: Ava Chen
Attendees (partial): Engineering org + representatives from Product, SRE, and Solutions Engineering.

Agenda:
- Quick wins & metrics highlight
- Team updates (Serving Runtime, Platform, Private Deployments, Console, SRE, Release Eng)
- Roadmap checkpoints and upcoming launches
- Risks / blockers and asks
- Action items

Highlights / Metrics:
- Latency: 95th percentile generation latency across hosted API down 9% week-over-week after kernel selection improvements in the runtime (measured on standard gen-1 benchmark).
- Cost/Token: Average cost per 1k tokens improved ~6% from improved batching heuristics; early Dedicated customers reporting ~4–5% lower unit cost in canary.
- Errors: Production request error rate steady at 0.18% (target <0.2%). Notable spike on 6/14 traced to an edge-case in model fallback routing; mitigated by a patch rolled at 6/15.
- Throughput: Dedicated pool utilization trending up as more customers adopt steady-reserved capacity; average queue latency in Dedicated fell from 320ms to 270ms.

Town Square Notes / Company News: 
- Reminder: Private deployment pilot for FinCorp enters validation next week — on-prem team to support (see Private Deployments update).
- New hiring update: SRE hiring loop for senior infra reliability engineer proceeding; top candidate onsite next Tue.

Team Updates:
1) Serving Runtime (Ravi Singh)
- Shipped kernel-selection fallback logic to prefer lower-latency kernels for short-sequence requests; initial telemetry shows 7–10% latency gains on small seq workloads.
- Open work: KV cache eviction policy needs tuning for multi-model serving — currently prototyping LRU with model-aware weighting.
- Blockers: GPU profiling tooling intermittently fails on newest NVIDIA driver; release-eng working on driver pin in CI.
- Link: PR #472 addressed earlier — microbenchmarks included.

2) Platform & Orchestration (María González)
- Autoscaling policy alpha deployed for Dedicated pools; policy allows scheduled scaling and burst override for high-priority tenants.
- Work underway: adding spot-instance-aware placement logic to reduce Dedicated cost by up to 12% (simulation stage).
- Risk: Scheduler recovery path under repeated leader elections needs a short-term throttling control to avoid cascading rollbacks.

3) Private Deployments / On-Prem (Ethan Park)
- FinCorp pilot readiness: network diagrams approved, KMS integration checklist complete. On-prem agent will be deployed in staging next Wed.
- Compliance: validating audit log retention and HSM KMS paths for EU region — small gap in timestamp formatting found (fix scheduled).
- Ask: Need an SRE on-call shadow for 2 days during first deploy (volunteer pool requested).

4) Console & Observability (Sharmila)
- New per-route cost breakdown landed in beta for 25 accounts; early feedback positive, more UX polish planned.
- Tracing hook added so that SDK-mapped request IDs flow through to Jaeger/observability. Need to document for SDKs.

5) Site Reliability (SRE) (Sam Taylor)
- Incident review: 6/14 fallback routing spike retrospective complete; action: add faster circuit-breaker for fallback selectors and increase alert sensitivity on routing mismatch counts.
- Reliability metrics: Monthly uptime target 99.95% — May rolled up at 99.96%.
- On-call rotation: new on-call escalation doc drafted; training scheduled next week.

6) Release Engineering (Kaya)
- CI pipeline: experimental GPU-driver pinning job added to catch driver/torch incompatible combos earlier.
- Release cadence: aiming for a smaller, more frequent release for runtime patches (biweekly) to accelerate kernel fixes.

Roadmap Checkpoints / Launches:
- Next week: Private deployment pilot (FinCorp) — soft launch, support window requested (see asks).
- 6/30: Beta of autoscaling policies to expanded Dedicated customers. Please sign up for the beta via the internal form.
- July: Eval harness improvements (quality regression tests with prompt sets) scheduled to merge mid-July.

Risks & Blockers (current):
- Driver/CI instability: release-eng to finalize driver pinning, ETA 6/19.
- KV cache eviction policy unknowns for multi-tenant bursts — serving runtime to deliver a design doc by 6/24.
- On-prem deploy shoulder support: we need 2 SRE volunteers for FinCorp deploy window (6/23–6/25).

Decisions Needed / Asks:
- Approve temporary on-call shadow budget for FinCorp pilot (2 SREs, 3 days) — Product to confirm funding.
- Priority decision on model-aware KV cache: fast/approximate LRU now vs. slower precise approach. Requesting engineering leadership call by 6/22.

Action Items (owners + dates):
- Ravi: Draft KV cache eviction design doc and circulate (due 2026-06-24).
- María: Finish autoscaler roll-out checklist and open beta invite (due 2026-06-20).
- Ethan: Coordinate FinCorp on-prem staging deploy and confirm SRE shadow roster (due 2026-06-19).
- Sam: Implement routing circuit-breaker tweak and adjust alert thresholds (due 2026-06-21).
- Kaya: Finalize GPU driver pin CI job and ensure compatibility matrix added to PR template (due 2026-06-19).
- All teams: Add one representative to the rollout readiness channel for FinCorp (Slack channel #finpilot-readiness).

Notes / Misc (working doc style):
- Quick reminder to link any urgent bug tickets into JIRA-ENG-8901 for consolidated tracking.
- A few suggested improvements to the all-hands format: keep updates to 3 bullets per team and use a one-slide status deck to speed the meeting.

Appendix (short links):
- Runtime PR with kernel fallback: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/472
- Retrospective doc for 6/14 incident: CONFLUENCE-PLAT-1423
- Tracking ticket for autoscaler beta: JIRA-ENG-8901

End of notes.
